vis_sources.name: Secluded Beach Foam
vis_sources.notes: On St. Martin's Day, Aquam vis in the form of sea foam is cast up onto a secluded beach.

vis_sources.name: The Secluded Pool
vis_sources.notes: Water collected when the image of the second full moon in a month is reflected in a secluded pool. Occurs about once every three years.

vis_sources.name: The Hilltop Weather
vis_sources.notes: If the weather atop a particular hill can be captured in a bottle of blue glass on midwinter's day, it becomes Auram vis.

vis_sources.name: The Leper Colony Bandages
vis_sources.notes: The discarded bandages of a certain leper colony are Corpus vis.

vis_sources.name: Tapestry Threads of Bayeux
vis_sources.notes: Golden threads appear among the embroidery on feast days. Must be plucked before vespers.

vis_sources.name: Mont-Saint-Michel Tide Pools
vis_sources.notes: Spring tide crystallization — salt crystals that form in the tide pools at the base of the mount during the great spring tides. Claimed by Sjórseiðr as the covenant's first prize pick, Tribunal 1223.

vis_sources.name: The Confessor's Library
vis_sources.notes: Marginalia manifest in monastery books — fresh illuminated letters appear overnight in the margins of certain texts at the monastery.

vis_sources.name: Channel Islands Source
vis_sources.notes: Disputed jurisdiction — Jersey. The precise nature of this source and its harvest method are recorded at Confluensis.

vis_sources.name: Cider Press of Domfront
vis_sources.notes: St. Martin's Day harvest. The first pressing at a particular ancient cider press yields a few cups of fluid that is Muto vis before turning to ordinary cider.

vis_sources.name: Drowned Village Bells
vis_sources.notes: Barnacles on submerged bells. A village swallowed by the sea long ago; the barnacles that grow on the sunken bells carry Perdo vis and must be scraped free by a diver.

vis_sources.name: The Diedne Garden
vis_sources.notes: Politically contested. An overgrown garden at a ruined Diedne covenant site still produces three unusual herbs each spring. Multiple covenants claim historical rights.

vis_sources.name: Pilgrim Road Stones
vis_sources.notes: Santiago route markers. Certain milestone stones on the pilgrim road to Santiago bear the vis — collected by pressing wax against the face of the stone on a feast of St. James.

vis_sources.name: Norman Barrow Frost
vis_sources.notes: Winter solstice hoarfrost. The frost that forms inside the burial chamber of a Norman barrow on the solstice is Corpus vis — it must be scraped free before dawn.

vis_sources.name: Shepherd's Stone
vis_sources.notes: Midsummer's Eve weeping. A lone standing stone in a sheep pasture "weeps" a single drop of moisture on Midsummer's Eve, regardless of the weather.

vis_sources.name: Market Cross Weather
vis_sources.notes: Specific weather patterns on market day. Once a year, a peculiar wind circles a market cross in a particular town. Captured in a sealed jar, it is Auram vis.

vis_sources.name: The Needles, Belle-Île
vis_sources.notes: At peak high tide when wind is from the west, the surf against a sea-stack cluster produces dense persistent foam unlike ordinary sea-froth. Collected in sealed vessel before the tide turns.

vis_sources.name: The Singing Stones, St. Malo
vis_sources.notes: Flat schist stones near the Rance estuary ring with a metallic tone when struck in sequence. The shimmer in the air captured on parchment pressed to the stone is Imaginem vis. Must be a still day.

vis_sources.name: Grove of St. Lié, Montagne de Reims
vis_sources.notes: Pale flowers bloom on a burial mound in early spring before anything else stirs. Petals gathered at dawn while still wet with dew are Creo vis. Wilt and lose potency by midday.

vis_sources.name: Ancient Oak of the Forest of Lyons
vis_sources.notes: Three golden-shelled acorns appear on Michaelmas and remain for nine days. Castle garrison considers the tree their property — mundane trespass is the obstacle, not magic.

vis_sources.name: Carnac Solstice Shadow
vis_sources.notes: At the center of the great avenues, one menhir casts no shadow at noon on the summer solstice. The absence, captured in black cloth pressed to the stone's base, is Vim vis.

vis_sources.name: Champ-Dolent Menhir, near Dol
vis_sources.notes: On the anniversary of the Schism War battle, red-brown dust forms at the menhir's base. Swept into a jar before rain falls, it is Terram vis. House Guernicus watches this site.

vis_sources.name: Roman Temple of Mars, Corseul
vis_sources.notes: Midwinter frost forms letter-like patterns on the inside of the ruined round temple walls. Scraped from brick before noon, this frost-water is Intellego vis. Requires entering the regio at dawn.

vis_sources.name: Gâvre Forest Leper Hospital
vis_sources.notes: The hospital burns its dead. Ash from these pyres contains Corpus vis if gathered before rain falls. The brothers are charitable but not blind — regular visitors invite Church scrutiny.

vis_sources.name: Crossroads Chapel, Champagne Road
vis_sources.notes: Travelers who confess their deepest secret to the empty chapel find a small rough stone on the threshold when they leave. Appears without pattern, ~twice yearly. Must be gathered before sunset.

vis_sources.name: The Basilisk Tree
vis_sources.notes: A tree in a forest has a basilisk family nesting in its roots. The fruit of the tree, if the basilisks permit collection, is Perdo vis.

vis_sources.name: The Ghostly Maiden's Song
vis_sources.notes: The mournful song of a ghostly maiden is Mentem vis. She must first be enticed to sing her lament, then the magus must capture the song in physical form.

vis_sources.name: The Falcon's Cliff
vis_sources.notes: A falcon nests on a cliff ledge every year. On the same day, a serpent tries to steal an egg. If prevented, the egg contains Animal vis. If the serpent succeeds, it contains Vim vis (if caught). Claimed by Sjórseiðr as a tribunal prize pick; harvested by Dagmar in Spring 1224 (Animal vis, six weeks worth).

vis_sources.name: The Siren of Décollé Point
vis_sources.notes: A siren inhabits the sea-cave near St. Malo. If persuaded to leave the cave willingly — not tricked or compelled — scales she sheds passing into daylight are Animal vis. She shatters boats in response to deception.

vis_sources.name: The Ghost Fleet of Barfleur
vis_sources.notes: On stormy winter nights, a spectral fleet passes Barfleur. The trailing ship's lantern still burns. A magus who boards it by ordinary seamanship and asks the captain where he sails receives a coal that is Vim vis.

vis_sources.name: The Faux de Verzy
vis_sources.notes: The dark dwarfs of the twisted beech grove leave behind bundles of Perdo vis — remnants of their enchantments. Must be collected at night. Faerie aura 4; Hermetic magic is unreliable and draws their attention.

vis_sources.name: The Boar King's Hunt
vis_sources.notes: Finding one of the Boar King's abandoned carcasses and reporting it to his court before the ravens do earns the right to harvest — the heart contains Animal vis. Taking without reporting is a grave insult he never forgets.

vis_sources.name: The Hague-Dicke Ghost
vis_sources.notes: An old Norse ghost recites the names of all he killed on the longest night. Listen through to dawn without speaking, and he says one true thing about your future. Written in Old Norse immediately, this is Mentem vis. Any interruption rouses all the ghosts.

vis_sources.name: Kerbourg Megalith Alley
vis_sources.notes: Two consenting magi perform certamen within the alley on the equinox. The loser's sigil pools in the capstone. Marsh-water held up to catch the drip holds Rego vis. The stones know if certamen is faked.

vis_sources.name: The Lutin's Sacred Fire
vis_sources.notes: Lutin servants of a Norman farmstead light a fire without wood in an old sacred well each winter. If a magus earns a coal from them freely — not by trade, compulsion, or magic — the coal is Ignem vis and stays lit for a year.

vis_sources.name: The Shifting Book, Abbaye de Jumièges
vis_sources.notes: Recovered "pages" (actually fish-skin) whose text shifts over weeks. A scholar who reads cover-to-cover and recites the changed passages from memory absorbs Muto vis, manifest as iridescence in their saliva for one season. The monks believe it a holy relic.

vis_sources.name: Ruins of Caput Capra, Loire
vis_sources.notes: On the anniversary of the youngest Diedne covenant's fall, a fist-sized lump of fused stone and ash appears in the ruin. Always in a different location. Confluensis apprentices visit annually — harvesting in their presence is diplomatically fraught.

vis_sources.name: The Branugurix Seal, Mount Dol
vis_sources.notes: The sealed entrance to the Diedne domus magna thins once yearly. Pressing a hand against the hillside and resisting the seal's pushback (Stamina + Magic Theory 12+) draws out Vim vis. Botching risks being pulled inside. House Guernicus actively watches this site.
